title: CLASS: Deep Partial Label Feature Selection with Cluster-Guided Disambiguation and Structured Sparsity

problem.claim: Partial label learning seeks accurate labels from weak supervision in settings where each instance has multiple candidate labels but only one is correct.

gap.claim: Existing methods typically use a two-stage process, can reach suboptimal solutions in high-dimensional settings, and lack effective feedback between feature selection and label disambiguation.

contributions.claim: CLASS jointly performs partial-label feature selection and candidate-label disambiguation through bidirectional optimization.
The method combines nonlinear deep networks for high-order semantic relations and feature interactions with linear sparse gating for label-specific, discriminative, and interpretable features.

A cluster-guided disambiguation module promotes inter-class separation and intra-class cohesion using distance constraints, confidence penalties, and alignment between predicted labels and class-prototype semantics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experimental results showing that CLASS outperforms state-of-the-art methods and is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: Partial label learning extracts accurate labels from weak supervision with multiple candidate labels per instance.

Existing approaches use two stages, may be suboptimal in high-dimensional settings, and lack feedback between feature selection and label disambiguation; they also face redundant features and disambiguation uncertainty.
CLASS addresses these issues with unified bidirectional optimization, deep nonlinear modeling, structured sparse gating, and cluster-guided disambiguation.
The authors report extensive experiments validating CLASS against state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects feature selection and label disambiguation through bidirectional optimization.

interpretation.claim: When coupled decisions influence one another, a jointly optimized formulation may address weaknesses introduced by a staged pipeline.

application.claim: Consider feedback-linked optimization for systems that must select informative features while resolving uncertain labels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when joint optimization is preferable to staged optimization across datasets or settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, evaluation metrics, numerical results, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, optimization details, or limitations.
